Senses.Explanation: To collect, hold, or restrain the mind rather than let it run after conditions. Hongren says to collect the mind without attaching to visions. Yongjia Xuanjue describes composed conduct as collecting thoughts; Yongming Yanshou also preserves the contrary warning that before entry into the source-mirror, even collecting the mind is mistaken. Elsewhere Yongming distinguishes concentrated contemplation from dedicated recollection. Cheongheo Hyujeong discusses collection of mind as restraint at the root, and Yuanwu Keqin advises a sick recipient to remain collected and unstirred by external conditions.
Senses.Note: The verb does not by itself specify posture or a particular contemplative system. Its object and purpose are supplied locally, and one retained authored passage explicitly criticizes mere collection of mind.
